title: Writing the verse to Monk's 'Round Midnight
summary: Monk came around the band from Minton's, and Cootie wrote the verse to 'Round Midnight, which is only on his record.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Well, let's just let that rest for a minute, since we're talking about Monk. Now, Monk's big number, "Around Midnight", I mean, you had a hand in that, didn't you?
In what way? What part did you write?
Well, I wrote the verse of it. And nobody never did play the verse, or interlude, or whatever they call it. Nobody but me.
No. Nobody made it on a record. It's on my record.
Well, how come you collaborated together?
Well, he was always around the band.
Well, at that time, he was working at Minton's, wasn't he?
Yeah. And so he'd come on up to dig the band.
No kidding. And so what did he -- I mean did he say to you, 'I've got something here. Do you want to put something to it?' Or --
Yeah. He wanted me to listen to it. And I listened to it. And I says, 'Okay, give it here.' 'I'll put the verse to it.'
And it turned out to be okay.
Yeah. It turned out to be a standard.
